newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable, despite ample allocation.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable, despite ample allocation.

text.p: Dutch money rates were stable on Friday and dealers said the allocation under the new special advances pact was ample, but this had no impact on call money.

The Dutch central bank allocated 4.26 billion guilders to the market this morning, with individual banks receiving 14.5 percent of the amount they had applied for, with the central bank setting a ceiling of 4.5 billion guilders on applications.
"We had expected an allocation of 14 percent and the overall amount was quite ample as well," said one dealer.
Nevertheless call money rates were unmoved, he added.He @
Overnight guilders were bid at an unchanged 3.12 to 3.18 percent.
The guilder was virtually unchanged at 112.52 per 100 marks compared to 112.525 on Thursday.
Dealers said business in Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs), short-term borrowing-instruments of the Dutch government, was thin at current price levels.
The July DTC contracts were set at 3.13 percent, the August contracts at 3.15 percent and the December contracts at 3.20 percent.
